newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia's Sihanouk seeks justice over jewels.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Sihanouk seeks justice over jewels.

text.p: Cambodia's King Norodom Sihanouk said he was seeking legal action against an individual who allegedly accused him of selling gems from a royal crown and a sacred sword.
The king, in a statement issued by the palace on Wednesday, called on his son, First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, to see that a Cambodian court gave full judgement on the issue.
"I can not excuse this extremely grave offence," the king said in the statement from the Chinese capital Beijing, where he is receiving medical treatment.

The king said that the individual, whom he described as a republican associated with Cambodia's 1970-75 U.S.-backed government, had recently accused him in a local newspaper of selling diamonds from the sword and crown.
The statement did not say where the two items were currently located.
The king said he was seeking Ranariddh's help in his capacity as his son, not in his capacity as First Prime Minister.
In 1970, then Prince Sihanouk was ousted in a right-wing coup. He was re-crowned King following the United Nations-supervised elections in Cambodia in 1993.
